transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-16
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Sam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Solutions), Maya Patel (NimbleVault - Platform), Jordan Lee (NimbleVault - Security), Eli Gomez (NimbleVault - Infra), Tom Wright (CTO)

Auto-summary: Quick recap at top, network flaps causing intermittent control-plane disconnects, planned upgrade to runtime v1.9.3 to address a routing hang and kernel fallback, agreed to run a post-change benchmark.

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription sometimes imperfect):
[00:00] Alex Rivera: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes today, um quick check-in on the private VPC pilot, main things on our end are the runtime patch and the routing observation you flagged last week.
[00:18] Maya Patel: yeah thanks Alex, we've seen two notable spikes in token latency last Wednesday and Friday that line up with the control-plane reconnects, so the engines would drop the KV cache and performance dropped about 30% for short periods.
[00:34] Sam Chen: okay that matches what we saw in traces — kv cache eviction on reconnect, and then a cold start on the model slice. there's also a route flapping event between your peering and the proxy subnet so the keepalive times out.
[00:52] Eli Gomez: to add, we did a change to our route table over the weekend — moved some NAT traffic to the new egress gateway, might be related. i can share the export after this call.
[01:06] Jordan Lee: um quick sec — from a security perspective we want to confirm the control-plane never sends customer data outside the VPC, is that still the model? the doc we have mentions 'optional telemetry'.
[01:24] Alex Rivera: good question. the control-plane signals are metadata-only by default and we can configure to not send any telemetry; we'll re-share the SOC2/compliance snippet. the private control-plane option keeps inference and KV traffic inside your VPC when configured, but we'll follow up with precise KMS and telemetry settings.
[01:43] Tom Wright: can you also confirm if the runtime upgrade touches the HSM/KMS integration? we can't have key rotation break in the middle of a migration.
[01:55] Sam Chen: the v1.9.3 upgrade includes an improvement to kernel selection and a more graceful KV cache hydration on reconnect; it doesn't change KMS APIs. we validated locally against AWS KMS and customer-managed keys, but we'll include the exact compatibility notes.
[02:12] Maya Patel: okay that's good to hear — last time we saw a delayed reconnect the service retried a few times and then blocked until manual restart, which was painful.
[02:25] Alex Rivera: yeah that behavior was fixed in a hotfix we shipped to hosted last month; v1.9.3 brings the same fix to the private runtime and improves route fallback so it won't drop the cache on transient egress issues.
[02:40] Eli Gomez: how disruptive is the upgrade? is there a downtime window?
[02:47] Sam Chen: it'll be a rolling upgrade per node; typical impact is brief (~30s) handoff for a node, but we do recommend a maintenance window for control-plane upgrades, we'll coordinate to minimize impact and run canaries first.
[03:01] Maya Patel: can we do the upgrade in our staging first? that's the plan but we want to run your benchmark script against staging to validate.
[03:10] Sam Chen: absolutely, we'll share the benchmark harness — it includes latency p95/p99 and throughput tests, plus KV-cache warm/cold scenarios.
[03:20] Jordan Lee: also need to see a diagram of the network flows — which subnets are egressing control signals and to which endpoints. our compliance team needs that for the audit.
[03:31] Alex Rivera: noted. we'll attach the architecture diagram and the network endpoint list into the CRM.
[03:36] Speaker 6: uh sorry, just to confirm, the route flapping you mentioned Sam, is that on the customer side or on the provider?
[03:44] Sam Chen: it appears to be in the customer's egress gateway path — we saw ARP/timeouts and the probes reported inconsistent next-hop replies. but the runtime fallbacks were a factor too.
[03:54] Eli Gomez: we changed the route propagation settings so maybe the route table didn't fully converge — could be a short TTL on the peering sessions. we'll pull logs.
[04:03] Maya Patel: one more thing — we've got strict security groups denying ephemeral ports, could that be causing some of the failures for the internal healthcheck?
[04:11] Sam Chen: yes, healthchecks rely on TCP on specific ports between the nodes; I think the security group they need is 10.10.0.0/16 allow inbound on 443 and 10250-10260 for the control plane. if those are blocked, you'll see the reconnect patterns.
[04:31] Jordan Lee: noted, i'll validate with the infra team. we use restrictive SGs by default so good catch.
[04:36] Alex Rivera: for the benchmark run post-upgrade, Sam do you have recommended concurrency and batch sizes?
[04:43] Sam Chen: recommend starting with small batch size 1-4 for latency-sensitive endpoints, concurrency 8-16 per GPU for gen workloads; for embeddings larger batch sizes help. use our sample prompts and the harness will sweep and produce suggestions.
[05:00] Maya Patel: on quantization — we tested int8 earlier and saw little regression, but some hallucinations crept in on certain prompts, have you seen that?
[05:10] Sam Chen: we have seen minor quality changes when moving to lower precision on some open models; Redwood Optimize can propose profiles: cache keys, per-route quantization profiles, etc. we recommend running a short eval set pre/post to capture regressions.
[05:27] Tom Wright: cost is a big driver for us too. if we bump up dedicated capacity after rollout, what levers do we have for cost control?
[05:35] Alex Rivera: batching, caching, and model quantization are the main levers. plus routing policies to route non-critical requests to a cheaper region or model variant. we'll share a cost/latency tradeoff doc.
[05:47] Maya Patel: any concerns about BGP or peering? We're using a cloud-provider managed peering, not full BGP.
[05:55] Sam Chen: that should be fine; just ensure your route tables propagate correctly and that the peering doesn't have asymmetric routing for the healthcheck IPs. asymmetric routes are a common root cause.
[06:06] Eli Gomez: i'll confirm with cloud support.
[06:09] Alex Rivera: switching topics — security questions we flagged last call: KMS key access and audit logs. Jordan, anything new on that front?
[06:18] Jordan Lee: we need to know whether Redwood stores any raw tokens or partial payloads outside the VPC, and how long audit logs are retained. our compliance policy requires 365 days.
[06:26] Alex Rivera: Redwood Private keeps logs within your control plane when configured; we can set retention in your account. for hosted we keep shorter by default but for private we can support 365 days retention and export to your S3. we'll send the detail doc.
[06:39] Jordan Lee: good, also we need a list of Redwood personnel who'd have access during an escalation.
[06:45] Alex Rivera: i'll include a list and RBAC roles — we support SAML SSO provisioning and can limit support access with Just-In-Time.
[06:54] Maya Patel: going back to the flaps, Sam, do you recommend changing the keepalive interval or retry counts?
[07:01] Sam Chen: increase keepalive to 20s and reduce aggressive retries on the client, but main fix is route stability; the new runtime handles transient disconnects better by keeping KV cache and doing incremental hydration.
[07:15] Eli Gomez: about the maintenance window, can we do a rolling upgrade outside business hours next Tuesday?
[07:21] Alex Rivera: yes we recommend off-peak — propose Tue 2027-09-21 02:00-05:00 UTC for a rolling control-plane upgrade; we'll do canaries in staging first and then prod.
[07:33] Tom Wright: please put that in the calendar and include the rollback plan.
[07:38] Sam Chen: rollback is a standard node-by-node fallback to previous runtime and KV restore from snapshots; we'll share runbook.
[07:46] Maya Patel: one more ops question — after the upgrade, will we need to re-establish any TLS sessions or certificate rotations?
[07:53] Sam Chen: no TLS cert rotation required; we maintain existing certs unless you opt for a cert rollover. the KMS keys remain untouched.
[08:02] Alex Rivera: ok, quick recap and then open mic for any other blockers. recap: Alex will share runtime notes and SOC2/compliance docs; Sam will provide benchmark harness and upgrade runbook; Maya/Eli will export network configs and propose maintenance window; Jordan will validate KMS and access list.
[08:20] Jordan Lee: streaming question — do you support server-sent events for streaming completions in private? we've been testing SSE in our app and curious if there are caveats.
[08:29] Sam Chen: yes streaming via SSE and websockets are both supported; in private mode you need proper route rules to allow persistent connections and slightly relaxed idle timeouts to avoid premature closes. we'll include the recommended NGINX/gateway settings.
[08:47] Speaker 6: there's a note in our slack about a 502 when the proxy health-check happens, could that be related?
[08:55] Sam Chen: yep, 502 from the proxy during an in-flight eviction is exactly the symptom; the runtime fix reduces those windows but route stability plus SG rules will solve it.
[09:05] Maya Patel: timeline wise, if we do the staging upgrade this week and prod next week, we should be able to complete smoke tests within 48 hours.
[09:13] Alex Rivera: sounds good. Sam, can you coordinate with Eli for the benchmark run and access?
[09:19] Sam Chen: will do. I'll send an invite and attach the script.
[09:23] Tom Wright: ok, from exec view i just want minimal user-visible impact and a clear rollback — if you can provide that by end of day Monday that would be ideal.
[09:33] Alex Rivera: we'll prioritize that.
[09:36] Maya Patel: small nit — in the previous run the KB cache evictions showed in the logs as 'k v garbage collect' typed weirdly, some of our log parsers mis-flagged it. did you change log strings?
[09:47] Sam Chen: ha yeah we had a naming rename in 1.8.7, some log messages changed; we'll annotate the log mapping so your parsers can pick them up.
[09:56] Jordan Lee: security follow-up — can you state who on Redwood will access our audit logs if we open a support ticket? we want to limit it to named escalation engineers.
[10:05] Alex Rivera: yes we'll provide a named list and RBAC roles.
[10:09] Eli Gomez: i'll finish the route export and send to Alex by Friday, 18th.
[10:15] Maya Patel: and i'll ask compliance for the specific KMS questions and post here.
[10:19] Alex Rivera: great, i'll follow up with docs and calendar invites. any other questions?
[10:24] Tom Wright: none from me. thanks everyone.
[10:27] Alex Rivera: thanks all, we'll recap in the CRM and action items out. talk soon.

End of transcript.
